values.DataCenterNotes: Kinder Morgan's first quarter 2026 earnings release says the Creekside Lateral is designed to serve growing power generation, industrial and data center demand in Central Texas. It says the project is backed by binding long-term contracts. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Kinder Morgan first quarter 2026 earnings release: the roughly 11.2 mile, 42 inch Creekside Lateral is designed to serve growing power generation, industrial and data center demand in Central Texas, supported by binding long-term contracts.

records.researcher_notes: Kinder Morgan's first quarter 2026 earnings release says the Creekside Lateral is designed to serve growing power generation, industrial and data center demand in Central Texas. It says the project is backed by binding long-term contracts. No specific data center is named.

ledger.note: EIA's data center language is on the 2029 Dalton Lateral Expansion II, a different project from this 2017 expansion, and no source ties data centers to the 2017 project.
The utility's and state agriculture department's project documents mention no data centers, and only opponents link the wider gas buildout to the Microsoft Mount Pleasant campus.

The project website, FERC page, Federal Register notice and EIA row name power and Mexico demand only; the data center remark comes from a local economic development official, not a project source, and no data center is sited.
Kinder Morgan's first quarter 2026 earnings release names data center demand among the drivers for the Creekside Lateral.
This is a 2004 expansion, only the EIA workbook is cited, and searches found no data center mention for this phase.
